metadata.title: Cardano Node And JorManager Tracing Final Architecture Tasks
metadata.description: Re-think the current transitional tracing implementation into the final elegant single-connection architecture anchored by task-500 research, then implement runtime tracing/data capture from core nodes using one muxed connection that captures all three mini-protocol families before JorManager-specific filtering.
metadata.importantNote: The final runtime design is one outbound connection per core node, one forwarding handshake, and concurrent protocol 1/2/3 loops that capture all data families before JorManager-specific filtering. Protocol 1 supplies dispatcher-backed chain/forge/KES/mempool metrics; protocol 2 supplies trace objects such as forged/adopted blocks and connection counters; protocol 3 supplies explicit datapoints such as NodeInfo and NodeStartupInfo. Task-500 research is the governing runtime architecture anchor; older sibling-session planning artifacts are historical inputs only.

phases.name: Architecture Alignment
phases.description: Replace the transitional sibling-session mental model with the final single-connection tracing architecture and pin the runtime boundaries before code migration.

tasks.title: Codify the final single-connection trace-forward architecture
tasks.description: Turn the newly proven protocol and signal findings into the accepted final tracing architecture for JorManager, replacing the older transitional design assumptions that remain in code and docs.
implementationNotes: Document the one-connection muxed topology, the protocol-family split, the source-derived datapoint manifest, the corrected NodeAddBlock semantics, the protocol 1 dispatcher-vs-direct metric split, and the live-proven dashboard signal inventory.
Treat the resulting research note as the architecture anchor for all remaining implementation work.
Do not treat the older sibling-session runtime shape as the final design after this task.
testCases: Research note references only findings already proven by source or tests.
Research note clearly identifies which dashboard signals come from protocol 1, protocol 2, and protocol 3.
acceptance: The research note captures the final architecture truth for tracing in JorManager.
Subsequent tasks can reference a single durable architecture artifact instead of scattered session notes.
tasks.completionNotes: Added the final single-connection architecture research note and live-proven signal inventory under task-500. This note now anchors the accepted tracing runtime design and replaces the older sibling-session mental model.

tasks.title: Refactor planning artifacts to the final tracing architecture
tasks.description: Update the tracing PRD and tasks graph so they describe the final single-connection architecture rather than the earlier transitional implementation baseline.
implementationNotes: Make the PRD and tasks reflect that the prior implementation work is now a transitional baseline, not the final accepted runtime design.
Reference task-500 directly from both PRD and tasks JSON.
Do not leave stale statements that NodeMonitor should remain centered on protocol 3-only datapoint sessions.
testCases: PRD architecture sections align with task-500 findings.
Tasks JSON phases and dependencies align to the new implementation sequence.
acceptance: Planning artifacts no longer describe the old transitional architecture as final.
Implementation sequencing is reset around the new elegant design.
tasks.completionNotes: Updated the PRD and replaced the old completed migration task graph with a new final-architecture task graph centered on the single-connection trace-forward design proven in task-500 research.

phases.name: Unified Capture Runtime Foundation
phases.description: Implement the production one-connection capture substrate and remove runtime dependency on separate ad hoc tracing sessions for different data families.

tasks.title: Replace runtime sibling sessions with one muxed tracing session per core node
tasks.description: Refactor the tracing runtime so each core node uses one connection, one handshake, and concurrent protocol 1/2/3 loops instead of separate ad hoc session clients and short-lived protocol calls.
implementationNotes: Reuse the live test harness topology as the runtime model: one connection manager owns one mux session and three concurrent protocol loops.
Keep protocol 1, 2, and 3 capture as raw families first; decoding happens downstream.
Retire runtime assumptions that DataPoint and TraceObject collection need separate sockets or separate long-lived sibling sessions.
testCases: TracingConnectionManager tests prove one connection can run all required protocol loops for an eligible node.
Reconnect behavior restores the full three-protocol capture state after disconnect.
Node teardown cleans up the single mux session cleanly.
acceptance: Production tracing runtime uses one socket per core node.
All required protocol families are captured concurrently on that one connection.
The runtime no longer depends on protocol-family-specific socket topology.
tasks.completionNotes: Finished the remaining runtime hardening for the single-connection tracing design: tracing transport eligibility is now core-only, NodeMonitor no longer manufactures relay tracing ports from promPort adjacency, the stale DataPointSessionClient sibling transport was deleted, and focused tracing/monitor tests passed with frontend tasks skipped.

tasks.title: Add production raw capture models for metrics, trace objects, and datapoints
tasks.description: Introduce explicit in-memory raw capture models and routing so JorManager retains all incoming protocol data before dashboard-specific or block-specific filtering.
implementationNotes: Model protocol 1 replies as raw metric maps, protocol 2 replies as raw trace-object batches, and protocol 3 replies as raw datapoint snapshots.
Do not bake current dashboard assumptions into the raw capture layer.
The raw layer should preserve fields needed for future tracing features even if current runtime consumers ignore them.
Do not turn this task into durable historical trace persistence or an archive layer.
testCases: Production raw capture tests prove all three protocol reply families are retained without loss of fields used by the current live harness.
Protocol 1 raw values retain counter/int/label distinctions or equivalent decodable representation.
Protocol 3 raw values preserve missing vs present datapoints accurately.
acceptance: JorManager has a production raw capture layer for trace-forward data families that all current consumers can share.
Later runtime signal extraction can be added without redesigning the transport layer or reintroducing protocol-family-specific sockets.
tasks.completionNotes: Added production raw capture models and routing for protocol 1/2/3, promoted protocol 1 metrics into production, moved NodeMonitor and block persistence downstream of shared raw capture, and recorded the freshness/invalidation boundary needed so stale capture cannot keep dashboard state looking healthy after teardown.

phases.name: Typed Signal Extraction
phases.description: Implement the production typed extraction layers on top of the raw capture substrate for the live-proven dashboard and block-monitor signals.

tasks.title: Promote protocol 1 typed extraction for chain, forge, KES, and mempool metrics into production
tasks.description: Move the test-proven typed protocol 1 extraction into production code so JorManager can consume dispatcher-backed dashboard metrics from the unified runtime capture layer.
implementationNotes: Port the tested parsing for chain, forge, KES, and mempool metrics into production decoders or signal services.
Respect the proven metric-name set and suffix scheme from the task-500 research note.
Keep direct-EKG-only metric families out of this task; they are not currently available from protocol 1.
testCases: Production typed extraction tests decode the same protocol 1 payloads proven in live tests.
Missing metrics fail safely without taking down the unified session.
acceptance: Production code can extract chain, forge, KES, and mempool metrics from protocol 1 raw capture.
The typed production model matches the current live test inventory.
The extraction layer consumes shared raw capture and does not own transport or reconnect behavior.
tasks.completionNotes: Added production protocol 1 typed metric decoding, added fresh-only metric snapshot reads in raw capture, and updated NodeMonitor to prefer the complete overlapping protocol 1 dashboard subset while preserving peer counters from protocol 2 or datapoints. Focused tracing and NodeMonitor tests now cover precedence, stale or incomplete fallback, and mixed-source peer behavior.

tasks.title: Promote protocol 2 typed extraction for block and connection-counter trace objects into production
tasks.description: Move the test-proven trace-object decoding for forged/adopted blocks and connection manager counters into the unified runtime signal layer.
implementationNotes: Preserve the already corrected forged/adopted block status semantics (`created` vs `completed`).
Keep connection counters sourced from trace objects because they are not currently available from protocol 1.
Keep decoding modular so more trace-object families can be added later without changing transport code.
testCases: Trace object decoder tests still pass for Forge.ForgedBlock, Forge.AdoptedBlock, and ConnectionManagerCounters.
Production signal extraction can merge chain and connection state from the same trace-object stream.
acceptance: Production runtime can extract block-monitor and peer-counter signals from protocol 2 raw capture.
No runtime dependence remains on legacy log scraping or on protocol 1 for peer counters.
Forged and adopted block extraction remains downstream of the shared raw capture layer rather than a per-feature transport path.
tasks.completionNotes: Added a shared production protocol 2 typed extractor for block events, connection counters, and AddedToCurrentChain fallback state; rewired NodeMonitor and TracingBlockMessageSink to consume it downstream of shared raw capture; preserved fresh-only fallback behavior; and documented the accepted Forge.Loop namespace compatibility plus forged/adopted hash-field contracts in task-521 research. Focused tracing and NodeMonitor tests passed.

tasks.title: Promote protocol 3 typed extraction for startup and structured node-state datapoints into production
tasks.description: Move the proven structured datapoint decoding into the unified runtime signal layer and align it with the corrected NodeAddBlock semantics.
implementationNotes: Keep `NodeStartupInfo` as the production source for epoch length, slot length, era, and slots per KES period.
Keep `NodeAddBlock` semantics pinned to epoch, slotInEpoch, and sync percentage only.
Do not reuse the old protocol 3 node-state-only model as the primary dashboard architecture.
testCases: Production datapoint extraction tests preserve the source-derived manifest and corrected NodeAddBlock meaning.
Missing datapoints fail safely without corrupting dashboard state.
acceptance: Production runtime can extract startup and structured node-state datapoints from protocol 3 raw capture.
NodeAddBlock is no longer misinterpreted as block height.
Protocol 3 extraction remains one contributor to unified dashboard signals rather than a standalone dashboard transport architecture.
tasks.completionNotes: Promoted protocol 3 typed extraction into production with a shared TraceForwardProtocol3Extractor downstream of raw capture, widened the runtime datapoint manifest so NodeStartupInfo is actually requested and retained, rewired NodeMonitor to consume protocol 3 through the shared extractor seam, and documented the accepted production boundary in task-522 research. Focused tracing and NodeMonitor tests passed.

phases.name: Consumer Migration
phases.description: Rebuild the current runtime consumers on top of the unified capture and typed extraction layers.

tasks.title: Refactor NodeMonitor to consume the unified tracing signal inventory
tasks.description: Update NodeMonitor so its dashboard state is derived from the unified protocol 1/2/3 signal inventory instead of the earlier short-lived datapoint-centric implementation.
implementationNotes: Protocol 1 should provide chain, forge, KES, and mempool metrics where proven.
Protocol 2 should continue to supply peer counts through connection counters.
Protocol 3 should continue to supply startup metadata and structured node-state datapoints.
NodeMonitor should no longer orchestrate its own separate protocol sessions or transport lifecycle.
testCases: NodeMonitor tests prove dashboard fields are assembled from the unified signal inventory.
Current NodeStats websocket semantics remain stable where practical.
acceptance: NodeMonitor depends on the unified tracing runtime instead of separate ad hoc protocol clients.
Dashboard fields come from the live-proven protocol family for each signal.
Peer counts remain sourced from protocol 2 where live evidence says protocol 1 does not provide them.
tasks.completionNotes: Extracted dashboard signal assembly out of NodeMonitor into the new shared TracingDashboardSignalService, preserved startup metadata availability without widening NodeStats, and added focused seam-level plus monitor-level tests. Verification also surfaced and fixed a live precedence gap so fresh protocol 2 connection counters now override protocol 3 peer values even when protocol 1 metrics are absent.

tasks.title: Refactor block persistence flow to consume the unified tracing signal inventory
tasks.description: Update the block-monitoring and tracing persistence path so it consumes forged/adopted block events from the unified trace-object capture service instead of isolated decoder plumbing.
implementationNotes: Preserve current candidate-block semantics and websocket publication behavior.
Keep forged->created and adopted->completed semantics intact.
Do not regress duplicate suppression or validation flow.
testCases: Tracing block persistence tests still cover both created and completed statuses.
Block flow remains consistent after unifying the signal source.
acceptance: Block persistence consumes the unified trace-object signal stream cleanly.
No isolated per-feature tracing transport path remains.
Forged and adopted block handling stays downstream of unified protocol 2 extraction.
tasks.completionNotes: Confirmed the live block path was already downstream of unified raw capture and shared protocol 2 extraction, then finished the remaining convergence work by registering TraceForwardProtocol2Extractor as a shared Spring dependency and adding explicit sink-level delegation coverage plus downstream BlockMonitor-preservation verification. No new block-signal service was needed.

phases.name: Cleanup And Final Verification
phases.description: Remove transitional runtime seams and verify the final architecture end to end.

tasks.title: Remove transitional session clients and stale test assumptions
tasks.description: Delete or simplify runtime/session code, tests, and active planning assumptions that only existed to support the older sibling-session or datapoint-centric transition path.
implementationNotes: Remove stale runtime assumptions before calling the architecture migration complete.
Keep the live single-connection harness as the enduring integration truth.
Clean up active docs or task guidance that would otherwise reintroduce sibling-session topology in later work.
testCases: No production code path remains that depends on separate ad hoc trace/data sessions per node.
Live tests still pass with the unified architecture only.
acceptance: The codebase no longer carries transitional runtime topology as an active design.
Tests align with the final architecture only.
Active planning artifacts no longer instruct future work to use sibling per-family sessions.

tasks.title: Run final live verification and synchronize docs
tasks.description: Run the final live verification suite against the block producer and synchronize final implementation notes into the plan artifacts.
implementationNotes: Use the single-connection live harness as the primary verification surface.
Record final architecture notes in the PRD/tasks/research area only after runtime truth is established.
Synchronize the PRD, prompt, tasks graph, and active research notes so future orchestration follows the implemented single-connection design.
testCases: Live clockwork snapshot verifies chain, forge, KES, mempool, startup datapoint, and trace-object block/peer paths under the final runtime architecture.
Planning artifacts reflect the final implemented architecture, not the transitional one.
acceptance: Final runtime architecture is verified live.
Documentation is synchronized to the final implementation truth.
No active planning artifact still presents sibling-session topology as the desired end state.

riskAreas: Migrating runtime consumers from the transitional session topology to the final single-connection architecture without regressing current live behavior.
Keeping protocol 2-based peer counters and block events intact while promoting protocol 1 metrics into production.
Avoiding reintroduction of protocol-family-specific transport assumptions in NodeMonitor or tracing persistence code.
Keeping the source-derived datapoint manifest and corrected NodeAddBlock semantics stable during runtime refactor.
summary.testingNotes: Keep the single-connection live harness as the primary architectural truth. New runtime work should not land without corresponding focused live tests or fixture-backed protocol tests that match the live-proven protocol 1/2/3 signal inventory. Do not accept tests that only prove a sibling-session topology when the production architecture requires one muxed connection.
summary.rollbackPlan: If the final architecture refactor regresses runtime behavior, temporarily restore the transitional runtime capture path from git while preserving the new test harness and task-500 research note as the architecture target. Do not roll back the newly proven protocol semantics or the research inventory.
